description: Compress a GIF by the only three things a GIF has — frames, colours and size. Nothing uploaded. Can you run shell commands? Then do not send base64: upload the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/gif-compressor (same tool, same answer, much faster). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

colours.description: Colours in each frame's palette, one of 256, 128, 64, 32, 16. Fewer colours make a smaller file at the cost of banding in gradients.

gif.description: The animated or still GIF file as base64. The result is also a GIF. Send the whole file as it is, up to 30 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. If you can run shell commands, do not write the base64 out yourself: send the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> -F <option>=<value> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/gif-compressor (add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" if you have one); the answer is the same JSON.

keepEvery.description: Drop frames to shrink the file: 1 keeps every frame, 2 keeps every second one, 3 every third. Each kept frame takes on the delay of the frames dropped after it, so the animation runs for the same time.

name.description: The input filename. The result is named after it with '-small.gif' appended to the stem.

scale.description: A size factor per edge, 1 being the original size. Over the API only 1 is accepted; any other value is refused, because scaling happens in the browser tool alone.

name: gif_compressor
title: GIF Compressor
